title: Matt LaFleur says St. Brown's 'mentality' sets him apart
headline: Coach says no Sunday concern for Watson or Golden, Josh Jacobs is ramping up with the next two days key, and Jonathan Ford has gone to IR.
summary: LaFleur said there is no concern for Sunday about Christian Watson or Matthew Golden. He said Jordan Love was beaten up after the game, took several hits, and was checked by the chiropractor, which is how the coach learned about his back. He described Josh Jacobs as being eased back in through strength and athletic training work, with the next two days of practice a big step toward full football activity. He would not commit to whether a player who had been limited would play, saying they would evaluate on the field. Jonathan Ford's move to IR surprised him, since Ford had been playing through an issue that eventually became too much. LaFleur called Jordan Riley's progress encouraging after a limited appearance last week, with more to be seen. He said he would not make much of Detroit's comments about its own improvement, and that his focus is on Green Bay's own alignment. On Goff, he praised the quarterback's decisiveness, poise under pressure, and trust in his playmakers, and said the key is moving defenders and not letting Goff set up comfortably. He also praised Amon-Ra St. Brown's mentality and said Detroit's Brian Branch would be a strong addition for their defense.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 22, 2026
headline: Saquon Barkley's return is still undetermined; Sirianni says it depends on how the week progresses, and Zach Ertz has been impressing in practice.
summary: Sirianni called Saquon Barkley a phenomenal player and captain, and said getting him back would be huge, but he would not commit to a timeline and said they will see where things stand as the week goes on. He said a run game that converts on third down keeps the play-action passing game working, and that the backs in the room have stepped up during injuries. On Jalen Hurts, he declined to discuss his timetable or the NFLPA's call for an investigation, saying he cares deeply about Hurts's well-being and that it is fluid. He declined to discuss the reported $250,000 fine or his conversations with the league and referees association. He praised Tanner McKee's intelligence and toughness and said McKee should keep rising, with every rep counting. On the offense, he said the staff must balance a system with attacking defenses using players' strengths, and that players matter more than plays. He acknowledged the team has lost four straight games and that it needs to get back on track. He praised Zach Ertz's practices and said he has had great reps with the first team and useful looks as a scout-team player. On the Cowboys, he said Christian Parker's familiarity with the Eagles is limited to his role in the building, since he was not in offensive meetings, and that film study is the main way to beat him.
